<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p11.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the normalized Lebesgue measure on
<math id="S3.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{r}^{d-1}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{r}^{d-1}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> .</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S3.F2.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="S3.F2.2.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18674v1/oneunitx.svg" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:236/194;" width="236" height="194"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>Area of perturbed patterns separated from <math id="S3.F2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> by a hyperplane.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p12.1" class="ltx_p">(i) If <math id="S3.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;a(x)&lt;r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;a(x)&lt;r</annotation></semantics></math>, then the perturbed input <math id="S3.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x+\xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x+\xi</annotation></semantics></math> is separated from <math id="S3.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> by the
hyperplane <math id="S3.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v,b}</annotation></semantics></math> if it is in the
polar cap on <math id="S3.p12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{r}^{d-1}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{r}^{d-1}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> centered at <math id="S3.p12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y=x+r\frac{p(x)-x}{a(x)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y=x+r\frac{p(x)-x}{a(x)}</annotation></semantics></math> with the angle <math id="S3.p12.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha(x)</annotation></semantics></math> such that
<math id="S3.p12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\cos\alpha(x)=\frac{a(x)}{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mi>r</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\alpha(x)=\frac{a(x)}{r}</annotation></semantics></math>
(see Fig. 2).
Thus by (<a href="#S3.E4" title="In 3 Probabilistic approach to robustness ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>), we get for <math id="S3.p12.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ξ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi</annotation></semantics></math> drawn uniformly from <math id="S3.p12.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{d-1}_{r}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{d-1}_{r}(x)</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p13" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\rm P}[\xi\in S_{r}^{d-1}(x)\,|\,f(x+\xi)\neq f(x)]\leq e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>P</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>ξ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.337em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm P}[\xi\in S_{r}^{d-1}(x)\,|\,f(x+\xi)\neq f(x)]\leq e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.p14" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p14.1" class="ltx_p">(ii) If <math id="S3.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(x)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(x)=0</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S3.p14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in H_{v,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in H_{v,b}</annotation></semantics></math> and thus the probability <math id="S3.p14.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\rm P}[x+\xi\in H_{v,b}^{-}]={\rm P}[x+\xi\in H_{v,b}^{+}]=1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm P}[x+\xi\in H_{v,b}^{-}]={\rm P}[x+\xi\in H_{v,b}^{+}]=1/2</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p15.1" class="ltx_p">(iii) If <math id="S3.p15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&lt;a(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&lt;a(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, then both <math id="S3.p15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.p15.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x+\xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x+\xi</annotation></semantics></math> are in the same open half-space separated by <math id="S3.p15.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v,b}</annotation></semantics></math>.
 <math id="S3.p15.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Box" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Box</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p16" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p16.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#S3.Ex13" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Probabilistic approach to robustness ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> analyses the local robustness at inputs in dependence on their distance from the hyperplane <math id="S3.p16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v,b}</annotation></semantics></math> and the input dimension <math id="S3.p16.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>.
The cases (ii), when the original input <math id="S3.p16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is farther from <math id="S3.p16.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v,b}</annotation></semantics></math> than the size of perturbation <math id="S3.p16.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, and (iii), when its distance from <math id="S3.p16.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v,b}</annotation></semantics></math>
is equal to <math id="S3.p16.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, are obvious. In these two cases, the local robustness at <math id="S3.p16.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> does not depend on the input dimension <math id="S3.p16.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p17" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p17.1" class="ltx_p">In the case (i), when the distance from the hyperplane <math id="S3.p17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v,b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v,b}</annotation></semantics></math>
is smaller than <math id="S3.p17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, the robustness grows rapidly with increasing dimension <math id="S3.p17.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>.
The probability that a Heaviside perceptron correctly classifies a slightly
perturbed pattern - lying at Euclidean distance <math id="S3.p17.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> from the original pattern -
is at least</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p18" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1-e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1-e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.p19" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p19.1" class="ltx_p">Thus the larger the quantity <math id="S3.p19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(x)^{2}d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(x)^{2}d</annotation></semantics></math> relative to <math id="S3.p19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2r^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2r^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, the more robust the network is at <math id="S3.p19.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.
The lower bound (<a href="#S3.E5" title="In 3 Probabilistic approach to robustness ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) illustrates the beneficial effect of input dimensionality on the robustness of a Heaviside perceptron.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p20" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p20.1" class="ltx_p">As a straightforward corollary of Theorem <a href="#S3.Ex13" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Probabilistic approach to robustness ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, we obtain the following
probabilistic bound
on the robustness of a shallow network with <math id="S3.p20.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> Heaviside perceptrons.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 3.2</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_{i}\vartheta(v_{i}\cdot x+b_{i}):{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϑ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}w_{i}\vartheta(v_{i}\cdot x+b_{i}):{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}</annotation></semantics></math> , where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b_{i}\in{\mathbb{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b_{i}\in{\mathbb{R}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,\dots,n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,\dots,n</annotation></semantics></math>,
be an I/O function of a parameterized shallow network with <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> Heaviside perceptrons,
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}H_{v_{i},b_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>⋃</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H=\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}H_{v_{i},b_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> be a size of a perturbation.
Then for every <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\setminus H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo>∖</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\setminus H</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ξ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi</annotation></semantics></math> drawn uniformly randomly from <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{r}^{d-1}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{r}^{d-1}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="S3.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathcal{R}}(f,x,r):={\rm P}[f(x)=f(x+\xi)]\geq 1-n\,e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{R}}(f,x,r):={\rm P}[f(x)=f(x+\xi)]\geq 1-n\,e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="a(x)=\min\{a_{i}(x)\,|\,i=1,\dots,n\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>min</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.337em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(x)=\min\{a_{i}(x)\,|\,i=1,\dots,n\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}(x)=\|x-p_{i}(x)\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}(x)=\|x-p_{i}(x)\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is the orthogonal projection of
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v_{i},b_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v_{i},b_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,\dots,n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,\dots,n</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<p id="S3.F3.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="S3.F3.2.1" class="ltx_text"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.18674v1/domain1.svg" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:314/237;" width="314" height="237"></object></span></p>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Robustness of a
shallow Heaviside perceptron network</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.p21" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p21.1" class="ltx_p">Corollary <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Corollary 3.2. ‣ 3 Probabilistic approach to robustness ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> shows that the local robustness at almost all inputs in <math id="S3.p21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> (up to a set <math id="S3.p21.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> of the Lebesgue measure zero) of a shallow Heaviside perceptron network increases rapidly with the input dimension, provided that the number of network units <math id="S3.p21.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> does not dominate the term
<math id="S3.p21.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}</annotation></semantics></math> (see Fig. <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3 Probabilistic approach to robustness ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>).
For example, this condition is satisfied when the number of network units grows polynomially with <math id="S3.p21.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Robustness of deep ReLU networks</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To extend our probabilistic estimates of local robustness to deep ReLU networks, we first
describe properties of their I/O functions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4.1</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\,{\mathcal{N}}(v_{l,j},b_{l,j},j=1,\dots,n_{l},l=1,\dots,L-1,v_{L},b_{L})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\,{\mathcal{N}}(v_{l,j},b_{l,j},j=1,\dots,n_{l},l=1,\dots,L-1,v_{L},b_{L})</annotation></semantics></math> be a parameterized
network with <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> layers, where the layers <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l=1,\dots,L-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l=1,\dots,L-1</annotation></semantics></math>
contain <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> ReLU units with parameters <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{l,j},b_{l,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{l,j},b_{l,j}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\dots,n_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,n_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{L}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{L}=1</annotation></semantics></math>,
the single unit in the <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>-th layer is the Heaviside
perceptron with parameters <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{L},b_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{L},b_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=\sum_{l=1}^{L}n_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=\sum_{l=1}^{L}n_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the total number of the network units. Then
the I/O function <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\mathcal{N}}}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\mathcal{N}}}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathcal{N}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{N}}</annotation></semantics></math> is piecewise constant on a
partition of <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\,{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\,{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> into convex subsets, such that each of them
has at most <math id="S4.Thmtheorem1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> faces, and each face is contained in a hyperplane.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span> For each layer <math id="S4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l=1,\dots,L-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l=1,\dots,L-1</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{l}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{l}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the function
<math id="S4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{l}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{l}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}</annotation></semantics></math> defined as</p>
<table id="S4.Ex17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{l}(x)=y_{l}(x)=(y_{l,1}(x),\dots,y_{l,n_{l}}(x))\in{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{l}(x)=y_{l}(x)=(y_{l,1}(x),\dots,y_{l,n_{l}}(x))\in{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{l}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{l}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> is the output vector of the <math id="S4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>-th layer.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To obtain the partition, for each <math id="S4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{*}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{*}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>, we construct a convex set <math id="S4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>, on which the I/O function
<math id="S4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\mathcal{N}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\mathcal{N}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is constant, and then
identify those sets <math id="S4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}({\bar{x}}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}({\bar{x}}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> that coincide.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We built the set <math id="S4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> recursively from a sequence of nested convex
subsets
<math id="S4.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{D_{l}(x^{*})\,|\,l=1,\dots,L\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="false" rspace="0.337em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{D_{l}(x^{*})\,|\,l=1,\dots,L\}</annotation></semantics></math> of
<math id="S4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>, that all contain <math id="S4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We construct them together with <math id="S4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> families of hyperplanes</p>
<table id="S4.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathcal{H}}_{l}=\{H_{w_{k,j},c_{k,j}}\,|\,k=1,\dots,l,j=1,\dots,n_{l}\},\quad l=1,\dots L," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mo fence="false" rspace="0.337em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{H}}_{l}=\{H_{w_{k,j},c_{k,j}}\,|\,k=1,\dots,l,j=1,\dots,n_{l}\},\quad l=1,\dots L,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S4.p4.2" class="ltx_p">such that the faces of each of <math id="S4.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{l}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{l}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> , <math id="S4.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l=1,\dots,L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l=1,\dots,L</annotation></semantics></math>, are formed by
subsets of the hyperplanes <math id="S4.p4.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\{H_{w_{k,j},c_{k,j}}\,|\,k=1,\dots,l,j=1,\dots,n_{l}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mo fence="false" rspace="0.337em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{H_{w_{k,j},c_{k,j}}\,|\,k=1,\dots,l,j=1,\dots,n_{l}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We start with the first layer <math id="S4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l=1</annotation></semantics></math>. We set <math id="S4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{1,j}=v_{1,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{1,j}=v_{1,j}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1,j}=b_{1,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1,j}=b_{1,j}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="S4.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\dots,n_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,n_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>
and define</p>

<p id="S4.p5.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\iota_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ι</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\iota_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> is either <math id="S4.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>
depending on whether <math id="S4.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{*}\in H_{w_{1,j},c_{1,j}}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{*}\in H_{w_{1,j},c_{1,j}}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> or

The function <math id="S4.p5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{1}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{1}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, that maps input <math id="S4.p5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> to the output
vector of the <math id="S4.p5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-st
hidden layer, satisfies for every <math id="S4.p5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\dots,n_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,n_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>

<p id="S4.p6.1" class="ltx_p">we get for every <math id="S4.p6.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="x\in D_{1}(x^{*},)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in D_{1}(x^{*},)</annotation></semantics></math></p>

<div id="S4.p7" class="ltx_para">

<div id="S4.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p9.1" class="ltx_p">So, <math id="S4.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{1}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{1}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> is convex, its boundaries are formed by
subsets of at most <math id="S4.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> hyperplanes <math id="S4.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{w_{1,j},c_{1,j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{w_{1,j},c_{1,j}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S4.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\dots,n_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,n_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, and on <math id="S4.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{1}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{1}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>, the functions <math id="S4.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{1}(x)_{j}=y_{1,j}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{1}(x)_{j}=y_{1,j}(x)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\dots,n_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,n_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, are affine or equal to zero.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Assuming that we have <math id="S4.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{l-1}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{l-1}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> together with the family of hyperplanes
<math id="S4.p10.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathcal{H}}_{l-1}=\{H_{w_{l-1,j},c_{l-1,j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{H}}_{l-1}=\{H_{w_{l-1,j},c_{l-1,j}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.p10.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="j=1,\dots,n_{l-1}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,n_{l-1}\}</annotation></semantics></math>,
we construct a family of hyperplanes <math id="S4.p10.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathcal{H}}_{l}=\{H_{w_{l,k},c_{l,k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℋ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{H}}_{l}=\{H_{w_{l,k},c_{l,k}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.p10.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="k=1,\dots,n_{l}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1,\dots,n_{l}\}</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="S4.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{l}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{l}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>. The function <math id="S4.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{l}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{l}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}</annotation></semantics></math>, that maps <math id="S4.p10.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> to the
output vector</p>
</div>

<div id="S4.p15" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p15.1" class="ltx_p">Setting <math id="S4.p15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{l,k}=\sum_{j\in J^{+}_{l-1}}v_{l,k,j}w_{l-1,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{l,k}=\sum_{j\in J^{+}_{l-1}}v_{l,k,j}w_{l-1,j}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{l,k}=\sum_{j\in J^{-}_{l-1}}c_{l-1,j}+b_{l,k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo></msubsup></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{l,k}=\sum_{j\in J^{-}_{l-1}}c_{l-1,j}+b_{l,k}</annotation></semantics></math>,
we get</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p16" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex28" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="S4.p22" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p22.1" class="ltx_p">So, <math id="S4.p22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{l}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{l}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> is convex, its faces are formed by
subsets of at most <math id="S4.p22.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{1}+\dots+n_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">⋯</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{1}+\dots+n_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> hyperplanes <math id="S4.p22.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{w_{p,k},b_{p,k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{w_{p,k},b_{p,k}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S4.p22.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=1,\dots,l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=1,\dots,l</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.p22.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1,\dots,n_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1,\dots,n_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the components 
<br class="ltx_break"><math id="S4.p22.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="f_{l}(.)_{k}=y_{l,k}(x):{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo rspace="0.278em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.278em">:</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{l}(.)_{k}=y_{l,k}(x):{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}</annotation></semantics></math> of the
function <math id="S4.p22.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{l}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{l}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{l}}</annotation></semantics></math>
that maps <math id="S4.p22.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> to the ouput vector <math id="S4.p22.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{l}=(y_{l,1},\dots,y_{l,n_{l}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{l}=(y_{l,1},\dots,y_{l,n_{l}})</annotation></semantics></math> are affine or constant zero.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p23" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p23.1" class="ltx_p">The I/O function <math id="S4.p23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\mathcal{N}}}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\mathcal{N}}}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>
satisfies</p>
<table id="S4.Ex34" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\mathcal{N}}}(x)=f_{L}(x)=\vartheta(v_{L}\cdot y_{L-1}(x)+c_{L})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ϑ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\mathcal{N}}}(x)=f_{L}(x)=\vartheta(v_{L}\cdot y_{L-1}(x)+c_{L}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p23.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.p23.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{L-1}(x)=(y_{L-1,1}(x),\dots,y_{L-1,n_{L-1}}(x))\in{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{L-1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><msub><mi>n</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{L-1}(x)=(y_{L-1,1}(x),\dots,y_{L-1,n_{L-1}}(x))\in{\mathbb{R}}^{n_{L-1}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
<math id="S4.p23.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L-1}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L-1}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> was constructed in such a way, that for all <math id="S4.p23.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in D_{L-1}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in D_{L-1}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</p>
