<div id="S4.p27" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p27.1" class="ltx_p">Setting <math id="S4.p27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{L}=\sum_{s\in J^{+}_{L-1}}v_{L,s}w_{L-1,s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{L}=\sum_{s\in J^{+}_{L-1}}v_{L,s}w_{L-1,s}</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="S4.p27.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{L}=\sum_{s\in J^{-}_{L-1}}c_{L-1,s}+b_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>J</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo></msubsup></mrow></msub><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{L}=\sum_{s\in J^{-}_{L-1}}c_{L-1,s}+b_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>,
we define</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p28" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex39" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex39.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})=D_{L-1}(x^{*})\cap H_{w_{L},c_{L}}^{\iota}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∩</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow><mi>ι</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})=D_{L-1}(x^{*})\cap H_{w_{L},c_{L}}^{\iota},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.p29" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p29.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.p29.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\iota" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ι</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\iota</annotation></semantics></math> is either <math id="S4.p29.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.p29.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>
depending on whether <math id="S4.p29.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{*}\in H_{w_{L},c_{L}}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{*}\in H_{w_{L},c_{L}}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> or
<math id="S4.p29.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{*}\in H_{w_{L},c_{L}}^{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{*}\in H_{w_{L},c_{L}}^{-}</annotation></semantics></math>.
As <math id="S4.p29.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> is either a subset of the positive or the negative half-space induced by the
hyperplane <math id="S4.p29.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{w_{L},c_{L}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{w_{L},c_{L}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
the I/O function <math id="S4.p29.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\mathcal{N}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\mathcal{N}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is constant on <math id="S4.p29.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>
(it is either <math id="S4.p29.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.p29.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> depending on <math id="S4.p29.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\iota" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ι</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\iota</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p30" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p30.1" class="ltx_p">It follows from the construction that for each pair <math id="S4.p30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p30.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\bar{x}}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\bar{x}}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.p30.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p30.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}({\bar{x}}^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>x</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}({\bar{x}}^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> are disjoint or coincide.
The partition of <math id="S4.p30.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained by identifying those sets that coincide.
 <math id="S4.p30.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Box" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Box</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p31" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p31.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> characterizes the input–output functions of parameterized deep ReLU networks with a single Heaviside output as piecewise constant functions defined on a partition of <math id="S4.p31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>
into convex regions.
Each region has at most as many faces as the total number of units in the network.
While the number of regions in this partition may grow exponentially with the number of network units, the geometric complexity of each individual region—measured by its number of faces—is bounded by the total number of units. This bounded-complexity property of deep ReLU networks is the key feature exploited in the next theorem.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 4.2</span></span><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\,{\mathcal{N}}(v_{l,j},b_{l,j},j=1,\dots,n_{l},l=1,\dots,L-1,v_{L},b_{L})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\,{\mathcal{N}}(v_{l,j},b_{l,j},j=1,\dots,n_{l},l=1,\dots,L-1,v_{L},b_{L})</annotation></semantics></math> be a parameterized
network with <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math> layers, where the layers <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l=1,\dots,L-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l=1,\dots,L-1</annotation></semantics></math>
contain <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> ReLU units with parameters <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{l,j},b_{l,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{l,j},b_{l,j}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=1,\dots,n_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j=1,\dots,n_{l}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{L}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{L}=1</annotation></semantics></math> and
the single unit in the <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>-th layer is the Heaviside
perceptron with parameters <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{L},b_{L}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>L</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{L},b_{L}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then there exists a subset <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\,{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\,{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> in the
form of a union of subsets of hyperplanes, such that the I/O function <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\mathcal{N}}}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\mathcal{N}}}:{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\to\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathcal{N}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{N}}</annotation></semantics></math>
satisfies for
every <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\setminus H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo>∖</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\setminus H</annotation></semantics></math>, every size of perturbation <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and every <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ξ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi</annotation></semantics></math> drawn from <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{r}^{d-1}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>r</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{r}^{d-1}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> according to the uniform probability <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\rm P}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm P}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex40.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\mathcal{R}}(f_{{\mathcal{N}}},x,r):={\rm P}\Bigl[f_{{\mathcal{N}}}(x)=f_{{\mathcal{N}}}(x+\xi)\Bigr]\geq 1-n\,e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">[</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">]</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>n</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{R}}(f_{{\mathcal{N}}},x,r):={\rm P}\Bigl[f_{{\mathcal{N}}}(x)=f_{{\mathcal{N}}}(x+\xi)\Bigr]\geq 1-n\,e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n:=\sum_{l=1}^{L}n_{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo rspace="0.111em">:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>L</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n:=\sum_{l=1}^{L}n_{l}</annotation></semantics></math> is the total number of network units and <math id="S4.Thmtheorem2.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(x):=\|x-H\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(x):=\|x-H\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

<div id="S4.p32" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p32.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p32.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof. </span> By Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, there exists a partition of <math id="S4.p32.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> into convex sets, each of
which has at most <math id="S4.p32.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> faces formed
by subsets of hyperplanes. Let <math id="S4.p32.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> be the union of faces of these convex sets.
For each <math id="S4.p32.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{*}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\setminus H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><mo>∖</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{*}\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}\setminus H</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.p32.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\mathcal{N}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\mathcal{N}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is constant on the set <math id="S4.p32.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> from the
partition constructed in the proof of Theorem
<a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> (see Fig. <a href="#S4.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). On each of these sets, <math id="S4.p32.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\mathcal{N}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\mathcal{N}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is equal either to <math id="S4.p32.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.p32.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>.
For a fixed <math id="S4.p32.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="S4.p32.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{*}_{1},\dots,H^{*}_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>m</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{*}_{1},\dots,H^{*}_{m}</annotation></semantics></math> be the hyperplanes, the
parts of which form faces of <math id="S4.p32.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>. By Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, <math id="S4.p32.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\leq n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≤</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\leq n</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p33" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p33.1" class="ltx_p">Using properties of high-dimensional spheres as in the proof of Theorem <a href="#S3.Ex13" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Probabilistic approach to robustness ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, we get for each <math id="S4.p33.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in the interior of <math id="S4.p33.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{L}(x^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{L}(x^{*})</annotation></semantics></math> and for each <math id="S4.p33.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,\dots,m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,\dots,m</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p33.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a_{i}:=\|x-H^{*}_{i}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a_{i}:=\|x-H^{*}_{i}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> the upper bound</p>
<table id="S4.Ex41" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex41.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="e^{-\frac{a_{i}(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{-\frac{a_{i}(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p33.2" class="ltx_p">on
the probability that <math id="S4.p33.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x+\xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x+\xi</annotation></semantics></math> is separated from <math id="S4.p33.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S4.p33.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H^{*}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H^{*}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
As for all <math id="S4.p33.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i=1,\dots,m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i=1,\dots,m</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.p33.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(x)=\|x-H\|_{2}\leq\|x-H^{*}_{i}\|_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(x)=\|x-H\|_{2}\leq\|x-H^{*}_{i}\|_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>,
we get</p>
<table id="S4.Ex42" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex42.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="{\rm P}[x+\xi\notin D_{L}(x^{*})]\leq n\,e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mi>n</mi><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\rm P}[x+\xi\notin D_{L}(x^{*})]\leq n\,e^{-\frac{a(x)^{2}\,d}{2r^{2}}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p33.3" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.p33.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Box" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Box</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p34" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p34.1" class="ltx_p">Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 4.2. ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a> shows that, for most inputs, the local robustness of parameterized deep networks
grows exponentially fast with increasing input dimension <math id="S4.p34.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, provided that the total number
<math id="S4.p34.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> of network units does not dominate the term <math id="S4.p34.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{a(x)^{2}d}{2r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{a(x)^{2}d}{2r}</annotation></semantics></math>.
This assumption is quite plausible in practical applications, where networks are typically of moderate size, and the total number of units depends on <math id="S4.p34.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> at most polynomially.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p35" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p35.1" class="ltx_p">Note that our estimates depend only on the total number of ReLU units, not on how they are arranged across layers, and therefore not on the network depth.
This is a direct consequence of the proof of Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, which relies solely on counting the number of faces of the convex cells
in the induced partition. By contrast, the number of convex cells in the partition does depend on the layerwise arrangement of the units,
a dependence captured by the notion of effective depth introduced in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite> for estimating the VC dimension of deep networks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p36" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p36.1" class="ltx_p">Inspection of the proof of Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> allows us to characterize the set of points that are susceptible to misclassification.
These points belong to a set <math id="S4.p36.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>, which has in <math id="S4.p36.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> the Lebesgue measure zero.
The set <math id="S4.p36.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> can be described explicitly by computing the parameters <math id="S4.p36.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{l,j},c_{l,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{l,j},c_{l,j}</annotation></semantics></math> of the hyperplanes <math id="S4.p36.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{w_{l,j},c_{l,j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{w_{l,j},c_{l,j}}</annotation></semantics></math> constructed in the proof of Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Robustness of deep ReLU networks ‣ Robustness of Deep ReLU Networks to Misclassification of High-Dimensional Data" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p37" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p37.1" class="ltx_p">The robustness improvement induced by increasing the input dimension <math id="S4.p37.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>
does not apply to points that lie sufficiently close to <math id="S4.p37.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>,
within a distance that scales on the order of <math id="S4.p37.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>d</mi></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{d}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For a fixed input dimension <math id="S4.p37.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> and perturbation size <math id="S4.p37.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>,
one can derive a condition on the distance <math id="S4.p37.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(x)</annotation></semantics></math> of a point <math id="S4.p37.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\in{\mathbb{R}}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>
from <math id="S4.p37.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>, which ensures that the probability of misclassification remains sufficiently small.
For a desirably small probability of misclassification and a size of perturbation, we can calculate the size of a distance from <math id="S4.p37.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>, such that the parameterized ReLU network achieves the required level of robustness for all inputs <math id="S4.p37.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> whose distance <math id="S4.p37.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(x)</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S4.p37.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds this size.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We theoretically investigated the susceptibility of neural networks to imperceptible pattern perturbations. We analyzed local robustness at the network input by quantifying the probability that a randomly perturbed input is misclassified. Exploiting counterintuitive properties of high-dimensional spheres, we derived lower bounds on the robustness of parameterized deep ReLU networks. These bounds on local robustness at most inputs grow rapidly with the input dimension, while decreasing only mildly with the total number of network units. Our results, therefore, demonstrate the suitability of ReLU networks for processing high-dimensional data.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To establish these bounds, we combined tools from high-dimensional geometry with the piecewise linear structure induced by ReLU activations. Consequently, our arguments do not extend to kernel or convolutional networks, whose robustness properties would require fundamentally different proof techniques.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Our theoretical analysis was inspired by the hypothesis proposed by Szegedy et al. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite>, as quoted in the Introduction. Our results support the first part of this hypothesis, assuming that the set of adversarial examples has an extremely low probability. We proved that if the total number of ReLU units grows only polynomially with the input dimension <math id="S5.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, then the probability that a randomly perturbed input is misclassified decreases exponentially fast with <math id="S5.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>.
As a consequence, such adversarial examples are unlikely to appear in uniformly randomly generated test sets.
Regarding the second part of the hypothesis by Szegedy et al., which suggests that adversarial examples may form a dense set (as the rationals), our results refute this claim for ReLU networks.
Specifically, any input <math id="S5.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> whose distance from the set <math id="S5.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> exceeds <math id="S5.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> admits no arbitrarily
close misclassified inputs.
All inputs within a ball of radius <math id="S5.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> centered at <math id="S5.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> are correctly classified.
Since the set <math id="S5.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math> is closed and has Lebesgue measure zero, there exist many such points
<math id="S5.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and radii <math id="S5.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, for which the ball of radius <math id="S5.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> centered at <math id="S5.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> does not intersect <math id="S5.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>H</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>

    <h2>Instructions for reporting errors</h2>
    <p>We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile
      support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the
      methods listed below:</p>
    <ul>
      <li>Click the "Report Issue" <span class="mobile-only">(<svg role="presentation"
            style="display: inline-block; vertical-align: middle; fill: var(--text-color);" aria-hidden="true"
            height="1em" viewBox="0 0 640 640">
            <path
              d="M224 160C224 107 267 64 320 64C373 64 416 107 416 160L416 163.6C416 179.3 403.3 192 387.6 192L252.5 192C236.8 192 224.1 179.3 224.1 163.6L224.1 160zM569.6 172.8C580.2 186.9 577.3 207 563.2 217.6L465.4 290.9C470.7 299.8 474.7 309.6 477.2 320L576 320C593.7 320 608 334.3 608 352C608 369.7 593.7 384 576 384L480 384L480 416C480 418.6 479.9 421.3 479.8 423.9L563.2 486.4C577.3 497 580.2 517.1 569.6 531.2C559 545.3 538.9 548.2 524.8 537.6L461.7 490.3C438.5 534.5 395.2 566.5 344 574.2L344 344C344 330.7 333.3 320 320 320C306.7 320 296 330.7 296 344L296 574.2C244.8 566.5 201.5 534.5 178.3 490.3L115.2 537.6C101.1 548.2 81 545.3 70.4 531.2C59.8 517.1 62.7 497 76.8 486.4L160.2 423.9C160.1 421.3 160 418.7 160 416L160 384L64 384C46.3 384 32 369.7 32 352C32 334.3 46.3 320 64 320L162.8 320C165.3 309.6 169.3 299.8 174.6 290.9L76.8 217.6C62.7 207 59.8 186.9 70.4 172.8C81 158.7 101.1 155.8 115.2 166.4L224 248C236.3 242.9 249.8 240 264 240L376 240C390.2 240 403.7 242.8 416 248L524.8 166.4C538.9 155.8 559 158.7 569.6 172.8z" />
          </svg>)</span> button, located in the page header.</li>
    </ul>
    <p><strong>Tip:</strong> You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.</p>
    <p>Our team has already identified <a class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/arXiv/html_feedback/issues"
        target="_blank">the following issues</a>. We appreciate your time reviewing and reporting rendering errors we
      may not have found yet. Your efforts will help us improve the HTML versions for all readers, because disability
      should not be a barrier to accessing research. Thank you for your continued support in championing open access for
      all.</p>
    <p>Have a free development cycle? Help support accessibility at arXiv! Our collaborators at LaTeXML maintain a <a
        class="ltx_ref" href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/wiki/Porting-LaTeX-packages-for-LaTeXML"
        target="_blank">list of packages that need conversion</a>, and welcome <a class="ltx_ref"
        href="https://github.com/brucemiller/LaTeXML/issues" target="_blank">developer contributions</a>.</p>
